claim: The acceptance criteria say that if `T` carries MessagePack attributes, they are honoured. They also say contractless mode applies only when `T` has no `[DataContract]` and no `[MessagePackObject]`. Without a surrogate, `Collect` always calls `CreateContractlessMembers`, which never reads `T`'s attributes. As a result, `[MessagePackObject]` with `[Key(n)]`, `[IgnoreMember]`, `[DataContract]`, `[DataMember]` and `[IgnoreDataMember]` on `T` are all ignored. An `[IgnoreMember]` property is still serialized, and integer keys become string-keyed map entries.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterHonoursTypeAttributesTests. HonoursIgnoreMemberOnMessagePackObjectType expects the `[IgnoreMember]` member `Secret` to be absent from the generated formatter. HonoursDataContractMembership expects the non-`[DataMember]` property `Extra` to be absent. On head both appear because contractless mode picks them up, so both tests fail.

claim: This change inverts the timestamp64 range check. The requirement asks for nothing in the runtime serializer. The original check `(data64 & 0xffffffff00000000) == 0` selected the 6-byte timestamp32 form only when the upper 32 bits (nanoseconds and the high seconds bits) were zero. The new check `(data64 & 0x00000000ffffffff) == 0` selects it whenever the low 32 bits of seconds are zero, then writes only those low 32 bits. Example: `DateTime.UnixEpoch.AddTicks(1)` has seconds = 0 and nanoseconds = 100, and is written as timestamp32 value 0, so the nanoseconds are silently lost. Ordinary DateTimes now take the 10-byte timestamp64 form instead of 6 bytes, which changes the wire format.

receipt_plan.detail: Serialize `new DateTime(2020,1,1,0,0,0,DateTimeKind.Utc)` and `DateTime.UnixEpoch.AddTicks(1)` with `MessagePackSerializer.Serialize` using base-built and head-built MessagePack.dll, then compare the bytes. Base gives `d6 ff ...` (6 bytes) for the first and `d7 ff ...` for the second. Head gives 10 bytes for the first and `d6 ff 00 00 00 00` for the second. Round-trip `DateTime.UnixEpoch.AddTicks(1)` on head; it deserializes as `UnixEpoch`.

claim: The requirement says 'contractless behaviour over public members', and the ledger (L3) ties contractless to `ContractlessStandardResolver`. That resolver serializes public get-only members and can deserialize through a parameterized constructor. The new collector instead keeps only public read-write members. It also rejects any class without an accessible parameterless constructor by reporting MsgPack007 (lines 77-81). Immutable or record-like types from Project A therefore lose members or cannot get a formatter at all.

On head the generator emits no formatter and reports MsgPack007, whereas `ContractlessStandardResolver` round-trips `P`.

claim: The timestamp32 guard now tests the low 32 bits instead of the high 32 bits. A DateTime whose seconds value is a multiple of 2^32 (for example 0, the Unix epoch) but carries nanoseconds takes the 6-byte timestamp32 path. It is written as (uint)data64 = 0, so the sub-second part is lost: 1970-01-01T00:00:00.5Z round-trips as 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z. Conversely, every whole-second DateTime that used to be timestamp32 (1970..2106 with ns == 0) is now written as timestamp64, which changes the wire bytes. This edit is unrelated to REQ-2129.

claim: When SurrogateType is null, the collector always uses CreateContractlessMembers, which reads every public read-write member. Any [MessagePackObject]/[Key]/[IgnoreMember] (or DataContract/DataMember/IgnoreDataMember) annotations on T are never consulted. A referenced type with [MessagePackObject] { [Key(0)] Value; [IgnoreMember] Secret } therefore gets a string-keyed map formatter that also serializes Secret. This violates the acceptance criterion 'If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured', and the output is wire-incompatible with T's own contract.

claim: needsCast compares m.Name against "OnBeforeSerialize"/"OnAfterDeserialize" for methods with ExplicitInterfaceImplementations. Roslyn names explicit implementations with the interface prefix ('MessagePack.IMessagePackSerializationCallbackReceiver.OnBeforeSerialize'), so the check is never true. It also only inspects type.GetMembers(), not base types. A data type that implements the callback receiver explicitly gets generated code calling value.OnBeforeSerialize() directly, which fails with CS1061.

claim: The timestamp writer mask was changed from 0xffffffff00000000 to 0x00000000ffffffff. This is unrelated to the requirement and breaks the wire format. Timestamps with nanoseconds==0 and seconds<2^32 should use the 4-byte timestamp32 form, but now take the 8-byte path or are mis-encoded. Timestamps with nonzero nanoseconds can hit the 6-byte branch and lose data. This changes serialized bytes for every DateTime and DateTimeOffset user.

claim: The contractless mode emits string keys but sorts members alphabetically and ignores read-only members, so wire order differs from ContractlessStandardResolver (declaration order, including getter-only members with constructors). Users who switch from the dynamic contractless resolver to this formatter get different map key order and a different member set.

claim: The timestamp writer mask in WriteTimestamp was changed from 0xffffffff00000000L to 0x00000000ffffffffL. The timestamp32 branch (6 bytes) is now chosen when the low 32 bits are zero rather than when the high 32 bits are zero. Seconds-only values (nanoseconds == 0) get routed to the 8-byte timestamp64 format, and values whose low 32 bits are zero are written as timestamp32 with the seconds truncated. This is an unrelated change to the serializer runtime that silently corrupts DateTime/timestamp data. It can also cause wrong data to be accepted or emitted across trust boundaries. The change has nothing to do with REQ-2129.

receipt_plan.detail: Serialize DateTime values such as 1970-01-01T00:00:01Z (seconds=1, ns=0) and a value with seconds=0x100000000-ish (low 32 bits zero) with the base-built and head-built code. claim: The change edits the runtime Timestamp writer in MessagePackPrimitives.Writers.cs, which is unrelated to REQ-2129. It flips the mask from 0xffffffff00000000 to 0x00000000ffffffff. The timestamp32 fast path is used only when the upper 32 bits are zero, so the new mask selects the wrong encoding and corrupts DateTime serialization. Numeric serialization is recorded as bug-prone in L16.

claim: The README and the attribute doc describe the contractless and surrogate-less formatter as serializing members under their names as string keys. Members are sorted by name and given int keys, but those are ignored for string-key maps. Contractless mode in this product also honours attributes on T, per the requirement: 'If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured'. The collector ignores [DataContract], [MessagePackObject], [Key] and [IgnoreMember] on T entirely. This is a requirement gap.
